APPROACH TO MENTAL HEALTHCARE USERS 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
MCHA FORMS  
 
o
FORM 22: if brought by police, to be filled in duplicate by 
SAPS officer – confirms condition of pt on handover from 
SAPS 
o
FORM 1: to commence with emergency treatment 
o
FORM 48: to commence physical restraints 
o
FORM 4, 5, 7: to admit as an assisted or involuntary user 
GENERAL MANAGEMENT 
•
Triage to 165 
•
Rapid assessment and sedation/restraint if violent or severely agitated – see AGITATION PROTOCOL 
•
Check vital signs including HGT, monitor O2 saturation if heavily sedated 
•
Comprehensive history and exam to exclude underlying medical conditions 
•
Investigations as per protocol – see below 
•
Hand over to Psychiatry on call if bloods/vitals/exam is normal 
•
Psychiatry to arrange rapid transfer to ward as soon as bed is available 
•
Pts will NOT wait in ED for additional investigations/management unless medically indicated 
•
Ensure that patient comfort is attended to – toilet needs, regular meals, smoke breaks etc. 
INVESTIGATIONS 
•
INDEX MHCU baseline investigations:  
•
VBG, FBC, UE, CRP, LFT, TFT, TPHA/RPR, (BC if features of sepsis) 
•
CSF – Chemistry, cell count, MCS, India Ink, CLAT, TB GXP. Add VDRL if TPHA/RPR positive 
•
CTB if indicated – low threshold for immune compromised pts.  With contrast preferred 
•
Urine tox if history or physical features suggest acute intoxication 
 
•
KNOWN MHCU baseline investigations: 
•
VBG, FBC, UE, CRP 
•
Further investigations only as clinically indicated 
•
Consider drug levels as indicated – anti-epileptics, mood stabilisers 
 
ALL FEMALE PATIENTS MUST HAVE A PREGNANCY TEST DOCUMENTED IN THE FILE 
COMPLICATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ANTIPSYCHOTIC DRUGS 
 
*EXTRAPYRAMIDAL SIDE EFFECTS/ACUTE DYSTONIC REACTION: fixed abnormal posture, oculogyric crisis, laryngospasm Biperiden (Akineton) 2.5 mg     
                                                                                                                     IV slowly, repeat every 2 minutes prn, max 4 doses 
*NEUROLEPTIC MALIGNANT SYNDROME: develops over 24 – 72 hrs, hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, rhabdomyolysis 
                                                                             Resuscitate, withdraw precipitating agent, supportive care 
CAUSES OF AN ACUTE MHCU DETERIORATION 
 
•
Underlying medical condition – 
sepsis/endocrine/rheumatological etc. 
•
Trauma 
•
Non-compliance 
•
Sub/supra-therapeutic medication levels 
•
Recreational drug/alcohol use 
•
Intracranial pathology  
•
Poor social support 
•
Pregnancy  
•
Acute psychological stressor 
Dr J du Plessis / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
